A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fused-Planes, with matching architecture, training procedures, and retained experiments. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original novel-view-synthesis results, training times, storage costs, and ablations on four ShapeNet categories and Basel Faces (Tables 1–2 and Appendix B).

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds mixed-class experiments, base-plane-count and VAE-initialization studies, rendering measurements, and representation analyses (Table 4 and Appendices D–E).

M1.justification: The micro–macro architecture, weighted shared planes, ultra-lightweight variant, losses, and rendering procedure are retained. V3 Appendix B and Algorithm 1 preserve v2's 500-object first stage and remaining 1500-object stage, including encoder freezing and latent supervision followed by RGB alignment. The revised main-text description and renamed training regimes do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: V2 evaluates models trained separately on four ShapeNet categories and Basel Faces. V3 retains these datasets and adds joint training on collections mixing two, three, and four ShapeNet classes (Table 4; Appendix C). This substantially extends the tested setting from class-specific sharing to sharing across heterogeneous object classes. The revised Basel-Face citation does not establish a dataset replacement.

E2.justification: V3 removes SPARF-32 and SPARF-128 throughout the quantitative and qualitative comparisons; these were prominent fast many-scene comparators in v2. Total-cost comparisons also omit CodeNeRF and its adaptation, previously included in v2 Figure 4, although their per-object comparisons remain. CodeNeRF-A is the renamed CodeNeRF (MSIG), with the same procedure and scores. These removals materially narrow the efficiency comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols include the seven-minute fixed-budget comparison in Figure 1, mixed-class collections with matched evaluation objects, tests using different base-plane counts, a reset VAE with 15% of training time allocated to warm-up, and FPS and multi-frame rendering measurements. The original 128×128 images, 90/10 view split, and training schedule remain; v3's 80-epoch second regime restates v2's 30-plus-50 epochs.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and training-stage comparisons, v3 investigates base-plane count and class diversity, dependence on VAE pretraining, fusion overhead, and what the shared representations encode (Appendices D–E). Individual-plane renderings, weight visualizations, and interpolation examples provide new mechanism analyses. V2's SPARF texture-failure case study is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-training run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V3's additional result rows retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: The retained aggregate and per-object NVS scores and original component-ablation values match across versions. V3 adds fixed-budget, mixed-class, base-count, VAE, rendering-speed, and larger-N cost results. For example, Table 12 reports Cars PSNR of 29.22 with the reset VAE and 30.27 with the default initialization. Reported Fused-Planes frame time changes from 0.36+9.71 ms in v2 Section 4.1 to 10.95 ms in v3 Table 10. SPARF result entries are removed.

T1.justification: V2 explicitly states the asymptotic feature-reduction factor F/Fmic and defines total training-time and storage models in Equations 10–12. V3 omits these explicit mathematical statements while retaining cost plots and adding tabulated totals. The architecture and optimization mathematics otherwise match after locating Appendix B; neither version introduces theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of improved planar-representation efficiency with similar rendering quality is retained. V3 narrows the broad multi-scene inverse-graphics framing to reconstruction of object classes and newly claims to be the first work improving Tri-Planes' resource efficiency. Its headline 7.2× training, 3.2× storage, and 1875× ultra-lightweight storage factors quantify retained results.

C2.justification: V3 expands the explanation of latent learning and shared planes to emphasize their joint role in preserving quality. It interprets base planes as semantic and residual components and discusses sensitivity to class diversity and VAE initialization. New Section 4.5 explicitly addresses bounded, object-centric applicability, fine-detail limitations, and difficulties with unbounded scenes. V2 has no corresponding substantive limitations analysis.

D1.justification: V3 adds dataset provenance and access information, a component-level storage breakdown, and technical instructions for the new VAE and visualization experiments. Core hyperparameters and the project link remain, while existing training details are largely relocated. However, v2's explicit sampling descriptions—four evaluation scenes per dataset and 50 scenes for ablation or training-stage comparisons—are removed.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused from the multi-scene-method taxonomy to Tri-Plane applications and compatibility with image models. V3 adds classification, editing, and Gaussian-to-image discussions, removes SPARF and meta-learning coverage, and sharpens the distinction from generic latent-NeRF pretraining. The newly named Schnepf et al. (2025) reference matches the work cited as Anonymous (2025) in v2.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Object-class terminology replaces the recurring MSIG framing, detailed two-stage training moves into Appendix B, and the appendices are reorganized. Dedicated limitations and reproducibility sections are added. These are substantial changes to existing exposition and structure.

P2.justification: The main document changes from two columns to one. V2's main comparison table is split into v3 Tables 1–3, Figure 2 is redrawn, and qualitative comparisons are recropped and regrouped. V3 adds a fixed-budget teaser and base-plane, weight, interpolation, and large-scale visualizations. Scaling plots are simplified, and the SPARF failure figure and comparison rows are removed.

improvement.justification: V3 better tests when sharing remains effective through mixed-class, base-count, and VAE-initialization studies, addressing conditions untested in v2. Explicit applicability limits and component costs also improve understanding. These benefits are tempered by removal of SPARF and CodeNeRF total-cost comparisons and explicit evaluation-sampling details, which weakens context and reproducibility. With the core performance evidence unchanged, the revision supports a limited net improvement.
